profile.campus: AWS Ohio (US-EAST-2) -- New Albany campus, Franklin / Licking / Union counties
profile.address: Newton Court, Amazon New Albany: Innovation Campus Way, New Albany, Jersey Township, Licking County, Ohio
profile.reading:
This building is one of the data center structures Amazon Web Services operates around New Albany, Ohio, a Columbus suburb spanning Franklin, Licking, and Union counties, the physical location of AWS's US-EAST-2 cloud region.

AWS's Ohio buildout has been documented in stages by the company, the City of New Albany, and Ohio trade and local press. The City of New Albany reported in August 2025 that AWS's cumulative capital investment in the area had reached $6.2 billion since 2015, that AWS had invested $19.7 billion across Ohio over that period, and that AWS operations in New Albany had contributed $1.4 billion to Licking County gross domestic product; the city's release also cited a further $10 billion in Ohio expansion AWS announced in 2024 and a forecast $23 billion cumulative investment by 2030. In August 2023, New Albany City Council approved a further $3.5 billion AWS investment covering five additional data center buildings, according to 10TV and Data Center Frontier coverage of that council vote. CoStar separately reported in 2024 that AWS's disclosed Ohio data center investment had grown by a further $10 billion. The City of New Albany's 2025 release stated AWS had completed and staffed two data center buildings in the area, with additional facilities under construction and expected to become operational later that year, and that AWS-related activity supported an estimated 1,550 full time equivalent jobs annually in Licking County and paid $3.1 million in property taxes and fees to the county in 2024.

AWS has not published a street address, opening date, floor area, or IT power rating for this individual building, and none of the city, county, or trade press coverage found for this page breaks the New Albany campus down building by building. This structure is treated as part of the documented AWS Ohio footprint described above.

profile.capacity_note: Not published by AWS at the building level. City of New Albany materials disclose cumulative investment, jobs, and GDP figures for the AWS campus as a whole, and report that two buildings were complete and staffed as of August 2025, but do not assign capacity, square footage, or opening dates to individual structures.
profile.facility_note: AWS has not identified this specific building by name, construction date, or operational status in any source found for this page. The City of New Albany's August 2025 release states two of the campus buildings were complete and staffed and others remained under construction; which category this particular structure falls into is not independently confirmed.

AWS does not publish a per-building street address, opening date, square footage, or IT power rating for this structure; none of the sources checked break the named campus down building by building. profile.regional_context: New Albany, a Columbus, Ohio suburb, has become one of the Midwest's fastest growing data center markets since AWS selected the area for its Ohio cloud region in the mid-2010s. American Electric Power's Ohio utility serves the corridor and has filed with state regulators over large-load data center interconnection requests as the New Albany, Licking County, and Union County buildout has expanded. Ohio offers a data center sales and use tax exemption administered by the state Development Services Agency, tied to minimum investment and payroll commitments, which local officials and trade press credit with drawing AWS and other operators to the corridor. New Albany markets itself alongside Intel's nearby semiconductor investment in Licking County as part of a broader technology corridor sometimes called the Silicon Heartland, and hosts data center campuses for other operators including Meta and Google in addition to AWS. Local governments in New Albany, Licking County, and Union County have negotiated a series of tax abatement and community benefit agreements with AWS, documented in city council minutes and covered by 10TV and Data Center Frontier.

reading.body:
AWS operates a multi-building data center campus in the New Albany area of central Ohio as part of its us-east-2 cloud region. The company does not publish individual building addresses or technical specifications as stated security policy, so this facility's specific power capacity and configuration cannot be confirmed from AWS sources. An industry index estimates the broader regional campus at approximately 500 MW of total capacity and operational status, though this figure is not independently confirmed by AWS.

The New Albany campus represents a sustained commitment to Ohio data center infrastructure. AWS and local government have announced a $3.5 billion five-building expansion and a subsequent $7.8 billion investment reported in 2023, with the City of New Albany crediting the combined footprint with $1.4 billion in annual contribution to Licking County GDP. A 30-year local tax abatement approved by New Albany City Council supports continued buildout.

Among Ohio's 76 mapped data center facilities, only 8 have published megawatt figures totaling 60.4 MW, placing this AWS campus rank 9 in the state by disclosed capacity. The lack of per-facility disclosure from AWS means the actual distribution of the estimated 500 MW regional capacity across individual buildings in this campus remains unknown and unavailable from company sources.
